Troubleshooting Steps to Trace the Tripping Issue of 230VAC MCBs
Check if the MCB is Tripped:
Inspect the MCB to see if it is in the tripped position. If it is, reset it and observe if it trips again.
Verify the Auxiliary Contactor:
Ensure the auxiliary contactor used for the status '230V fuse OK' is functioning properly.
Inspect Auxiliary Contactors:
Check the functionality of all auxiliary contactors (FC16, FC18, FC20, FC220). They should be working according to the MCB status. (If the MCB is on then its contactor should close respectively)
Check Downstream Circuits:
Examine all downstream circuits that are connected to AC components in the charger. This includes:
Main AC Fan
Main Heater
3VA Motor Switch
Maintenance Socket
Identify Common Causes for MCB Tripping:
Overload Protection: Determine if an overload condition is causing the MCB to trip by checking if the current exceeds the MCB’s rated capacity.
Short-Circuit Situations: Look for signs of short circuits, which are sudden surges of current flowing through a low-resistance path.
Electrical Faults and External Influences: Investigate other factors such as voltage spikes, faulty appliances, or damaged wiring that could cause the MCB to trip.
Isolate and Test Components:
Isolate each AC component (e.g., main AC fan, main heater) and test them individually to identify if a specific component is causing the issue.
Check Connections and Wiring:
Inspect all electrical connections and wiring for signs of wear, damage, or loose connections that might be contributing to the tripping issue.
Check Short circuit situation
Examine all downstream circuits that are connected to AC components in the charger. This includes:

Main Heater
3VA Motor Switch
